questions.question:
a) With the help of transmission line and data given below, calculate the RI level of each phase at point M at $500 \text{ KHZ}$ in fair weather condition using CIGRE formula. Also calculate the RI level of the line. [12]

Nominal voltage = $330 \text{ KV}$
Bundle spacing = $45.72 \text{ cm}$
Conductor diameter = $30 \text{ mm}$
Number of conductors per phase = $2$
Maximum surface gradient at central and outer phases at 330 KV are $1710 \text{ KV/m}$ and $1600 \text{ KV/m}$ respectively.
The CIGRE formula is given by
$$RI_i(\text{dB}) = 3.5E_m + 6d - 33 \log_{10}\left(\frac{d_i}{20}\right) - 30$$
Where $E_m$ in $\text{KV/cm}$, $d$ in $\text{cm}$, $D_i$ in $\text{m}$. [8]

questions.question:
Using the single-phase equivalent lumped parameter model circuit of a 3 phase, $400\text{KV}$, $50\text{HZ}$, $400\text{ km}$ long EHV transmission line shown below in figure, compute:

a) The maximum per unit switching over voltage while closing the main CB without external switching resistance $R_s$ considering the trap charge across the capacitor as $-1\text{ pu}$.

b) Switching resistance $R_s$ to be inserted during the closing of the CB so that the maximum switching over voltage in part (a) will be limited to $1.8\text{ pu}$.

Switching over voltage is given as
$$ (E - V_0) \left[ 1 - e^{-\alpha t} \frac{\sqrt{\alpha^2 + w^2}}{w} \cos(wt - \phi) \right] + V_0 $$
Where, $\tan\phi = \alpha/w \quad \phi = \tan^{-1} \alpha/w$

(ii) What will be the values at 1 MHz?
Formula: $\text{RI} = 3.5g_m + 6d - 33\log_{10}(D_i/20) - 30$
